title: Exact quantum circuits for a Heisenberg triangle with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction
abstract: We construct exact quantum circuits for a three-spin Heisenberg triangle with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction. A change of basis reduces pure DM evolution with arbitrary couplings to two single-qubit rotations, giving a circuit with at most 8 CNOT gates. When $J$ and $D$ are each the same on all bonds, one fixed basis gives a circuit with at most 10 CNOT gates for any real $J,D,t$. Local spin rotations extend the construction to a family with unequal DM couplings and nonzero exchange, requiring at most 14 CNOT gates. All circuits act on the full Hilbert space. An alternative pure DM implementation uses five two-qubit DM gates: analytically retuning the angles of one symmetric Strang step makes it exact. A 12-spin kagome example illustrates the use of these exact local blocks in lattice simulation.
summary: This paper develops highly efficient, exact quantum circuits to simulate the dynamics of a Heisenberg triangle model incorporating Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. By employing basis transformations, the authors achieve low CNOT gate counts for both pure DM and full coupling regimes. This work is crucial for advancing digital quantum simulation of frustrated magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct exact quantum circuits for simulating the time evolution of a three-spin Heisenberg triangle system that includes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction.
main_result: Exact circuits were derived for various coupling regimes, requiring at most 8 CNOT gates for pure DM evolution and at most 14 CNOT gates for the full evolution with unequal couplings.
method: The authors utilized basis transformations and local spin rotations to decompose the time evolution operator into a sequence of fundamental quantum gates, minimizing the required CNOT count.
model_or_system: The system is a three-spin Heisenberg triangle governed by a Hamiltonian combining isotropic exchange ($J$) and the DM interaction ($D_{ij}$). The results are tested on a 12-spin kagome lattice.
key_observables: The circuit complexity measured by the number of CNOT gates, and physical observables like transverse magnetization $\langle X_1(t) angle$.
important_parameters: The coupling constants $J$ (exchange) and $D_{ij}$ (DM coupling), and the target accuracy for simulation.
main_assumptions: The constructions provide *exact* circuits, meaning the gate count is independent of the evolution time. Time splitting remains approximate when simulating neighboring triangles on the kagome lattice.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exact evolution circuits for pure DM and equal Heisenberg-DM bonds, comparing the gate counts to approximate methods like Strang splitting. Figure 6 shows the 12-spin kagome cluster used for testing.
paper_structure: The paper details the Hamiltonian, derives the circuit decompositions for pure DM and full evolution using basis changes, and then applies these local exact blocks to simulate larger structures like the kagome lattice.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, gate-efficient blueprints for simulating complex magnetic interactions (like DM coupling) on quantum hardware, directly addressing resource estimation for quantum simulation.

Figure 3: Exact evolution under the Hamiltonian (2.1) using the basis change shown in Fig. 2. (a) Pure DM, J = 0, with arbitrary couplings: 8 CNOT gates. (b) Equal Heisenberg–DM bonds, with W0 = W(1, 1, 1): 10 CNOT gates. Each basis-change block contains 4 CNOT gates. The central rotations describe evolution in the transformed basis; the CNOT pair in (b) implements R(12) ZZ (φ).
Figure 4: (a) Exact evolution of the whole DM triangle for the analytical angles A, B, C of Eq. (A.8). (b) Implementation of a single DM gate with 2 CNOT gates.

Figure 5: (a) Directional transfer in a pure DM triangle: J = 0, all Dij = D > 0, initial state |100⟩. (b) Transverse magnetization in the full model (4.2) from |+00⟩. Solid lines: exact reference evolution. Open markers: exact quantum circuits. Dashed lines: one symmetric Strang step over the three full bonds. The dashed curve in panel (a) uses the linear parameters AS, BS, CS. Replacing them by the analytical angles in Eq. (A.8) reproduces the exact curve with the same 10 CNOT gates. The exact circuits require at most 8 and 14 CNOT gates in (a) and (b); the Strang circuits require at most 10 and 15, respectively.

Figure 6: The 12-spin periodic kagome cluster used in the calculation. The star shows six triangles; the two triangles on the right complete the periodic bonds. Repeated node labels denote the same spins, so the full cluster contains four upward and four downward triangles. Blue and orange triangles carry couplings (J, D) and (εJ, εD), respectively. Arrows specify the cyclic DM orientations.
